monthly_review.summary: You've shifted toward higher-intensity running this month, with faster paces and more time in Zones 3–4, but at the cost of reduced volume and lower aerobic efficiency compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Your cadence increased by 6 spm while vertical oscillation rose modestly (7.6 → 8.4 cm), suggesting improved neuromuscular coordination but potentially less economical form under fatigue during faster efforts.

goal_tracker.message: You need 19.3 more km across 4 sessions in the remaining 19 days — averaging 4.8 km per session — to match last month’s volume. Prioritize consistency over intensity: 3 Zone 2 runs (5–6 km each) and 1 mixed-effort run (e.g., 3 km Z2 + 2 km Z3) will achieve this sustainably.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite higher HR and pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.95 — a meaningful gain — even as average HR increased +8 bpm and pace improved by 43 sec/km. This suggests better metabolic coupling and stride economy at higher intensities, likely driven by your recent Z3/Z4 work (24% and 22% of June time vs 19% and 3% in May).

insights.title: Zone distribution flipped toward threshold work
insights.body: Z1+Z2 dropped from 79% to 51% of total time, while Z3+Z4 surged from 22% to 46%. This reflects a deliberate shift toward lactate threshold development — beneficial for race pace — but risks under-fueling aerobic base if sustained without recovery or easy volume.

insights.title: Cadence and ground contact time improved selectively
insights.body: Cadence rose from 146 to 152 spm, and your fastest recent run (6:32 min/km on 2026-06-11) achieved 162 spm with reduced ground contact time (274 ms vs monthly avg 314 ms), indicating strong neuromuscular readiness — but only during short, high-cadence efforts; longer runs (e.g., 11.1 km) stayed at 153 spm and 314 ms.

insights.title: Aerobic TE remained stable despite intensity shift
insights.body: Avg aerobic training effect held at 2.6 (June) vs 2.7 (May), even with 19 fewer km and +8 bpm average HR — confirming that quality (especially your 11.1 km long run at 3.4 TE) compensated for reduced quantity, though sustainability requires careful recovery monitoring.

recommendations.action: Do a 5.0 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) within next 48 hours, focusing on maintaining ≥150 spm and ground contact <300 ms using real-time cadence feedback.
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 2 time dropped to 31% (vs 43% last month), and your most recent Z2 effort (2026-06-04, 1.0 km @ 9:19 min/km, 137 bpm) was just above target — reinforcing the need to re-establish low-HR discipline.

recommendations.action: Repeat your 11.1 km long run next week, but hold average HR ≤140 bpm (not 141) and aim for cadence ≥154 spm throughout.
recommendations.reason: Your longest run delivered 3.4 TE — excellent stimulus — but HR was 1 bpm above optimal for aerobic endurance; tightening that margin improves mitochondrial adaptation without overstressing recovery.

recommendations.action: Add 2 × 30-sec strides (at ~392 sec/km pace) after your next two easy runs, focusing on landing midfoot with vertical oscillation ≤7.5 cm.
recommendations.reason: Your best pace (392 sec/km) occurred once, and vertical oscillation spiked to 9.2 cm during your fastest 1.0 km effort — indicating opportunity to reinforce efficient mechanics at speed without added fatigue.

weekly_focus.description: Reconnect high-quality Zone 2 work with precise form cues to stabilize HR, reinforce efficiency gains, and prepare for sustainable intensity increases in July.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥150 spm)
11 km long run (HR ≤140 bpm, cadence ≥154 spm)
3 km easy + 2 × 30-sec strides (focus: midfoot landing, VO ≤7.5 cm)
